issues.legal_issue: Land freed in perpetuity from land-revenue assessment by a capitalized lump-sum payment does not satisfy the land-revenue condition in the definition of agricultural income.
material_facts: The land was used for agricultural purposes, and its agricultural use was not disputed.
After acquisition, the land was treated as bearing a recurring land-revenue liability, which was redeemed by a lump-sum payment equal to the capitalized value of the revenue.
The conveyance subsequently vested the land free and clear of all government land revenue, and no land revenue was thereafter demanded or demandable from it.
issues.conclusion: The land was no longer assessed to land revenue after the redemption, so income derived from it was not agricultural income within section 2(1)(a) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(1)(a) requires both agricultural use and that the land be assessed to land revenue or subject to the specified local rate. A lump-sum payment that redeems the entire land-revenue liability and extinguishes future demands leaves the land free from assessment, so the agricultural-use condition alone is insufficient. The Court distinguished The Collector of Bombay v. Nusserwanji Rattanji Mistri and Others, [1955] 1 S.C.R. 1311, which concerned different tenure and acquisition circumstances.

rule.if: agricultural_income_tax_dispute and land_used_for_agriculture and land_revenue_redeemed_by_capital_payment and future_revenue_demand_extinguished

predicates.agricultural_income_tax_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether income from land qualifies as agricultural income for income-tax purposes.
predicates.land_used_for_agriculture: The land from which the income was derived was used for agricultural purposes.
predicates.land_revenue_redeemed_by_capital_payment: A lump-sum payment was made to redeem the land-revenue liability attributed to the land.
predicates.future_revenue_demand_extinguished: The redemption and the ensuing grant left no land revenue thereafter demanded or demandable from the land.

issues.definition: When an agricultural-income tax dispute concerns agricultural land whose revenue liability was redeemed by a capital payment and whose future revenue demands were extinguished, the income is not agricultural income under the definition.
